arxiv-2106-05305.title: Linear growth of quantum circuit complexity
arxiv-2106-05305.creator: Jonas Haferkamp, Philippe Faist, Naga B. T. Kothakonda, Jens Eisert, Nicole Yunger Halpern
arxiv-2106-05305.description: Abstract Quantifying quantum states’ complexity is a key problem in various subfields of science, from quantum computing to black-hole physics. We prove a prominent conjecture by Brown and Susskind about how random quantum circuits’ complexity increases. Consider constructing a unitary from Haar-random two-qubit quantum gates.

arxiv-2206-03142.creator: Qianhang Ding
arxiv-2206-03142.description: Abstract We propose that primordial black hole (PBH) binary systems can lead to standard timers in tracking the evolution of the Universe. Through gravitational waves from monochromatic PBH binaries, the probability distribution on major axis and eccentricity from the same redshift is obtained.

arxiv-2404-17011.title: First-Fit Coloring of Forests in Random Arrival Model
arxiv-2404-17011.creator: Bartłomiej Bosek, Grzegorz Gutowski, Michał Lasoń, Jakub Przybyło
arxiv-2404-17011.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Bartłomiej Bosek, Grzegorz Gutowski, Michał Lasoń, Jakub Przybyło. We consider a graph coloring algorithm that processes vertices in order taken uniformly at random and assigns colors to them using First-Fit strategy. We show that this algorithm uses, in expectation, at most ( 1 + o ⁡ ( 1 ) ) ⋅ ln ⁡ n / ln ⁡ ln ⁡ n (1+o{\left(1\right)})\cdot\ln n\,/\ln\ln n different colors to color any forest with n n vertices.

arxiv-2405-04083.title: On the representation of C-recursive integer sequences by arithmetic terms
arxiv-2405-04083.creator: Mihai Prunescu, Lorenzo Sauras-Altuzarra
arxiv-2405-04083.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mihai Prunescu, Lorenzo Sauras-Altuzarra. We show that, if an integer sequence is given by a linear recurrence of constant rational coefficients, then it can be represented by the difference of two arithmetic terms that do not contain any irrational constant. We apply our methods to various Lucas sequences (including the classical Fibonacci sequence), to the sequence of solutions of Pell’s equation and to some other C-recursive sequences of order three. AMS Subject Classification: 39A06 (primary), 11B37, 11B39.

arxiv-2409-05725.title: Spectral and Homological Bounds on k-Component Edge Connectivity
arxiv-2409-05725.creator: Joshua Steier
arxiv-2409-05725.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Joshua Steier. We present a novel theoretical framework connecting k-component edge connectivity with spectral graph theory and homology theory to provide new insights into the resilience of real-world networks. By extending classical edge connectivity to higher-dimensional simplicial complexes, we derive tight spectral-homological bounds on the minimum number of edges that must be removed to ensure that all remaining components in the graph have size less than k k .

arxiv-2411-06767.title: PDC & DM-SFT: A Road for LLM SQL Bug-Fix Enhancing
arxiv-2411-06767.creator: Yiwen Duan, Yonghong Yu, Xiaoming Zhao, Yichang Wu, Wenbo Liu
arxiv-2411-06767.description: Abstract Code Large Language Models (Code LLMs), such as Code llama and DeepSeek-Coder, have demonstrated exceptional performance in the code generation tasks. However, most existing models focus on the abilities of generating correct code, but often struggle with bug repair. We introduce a suit of methods to enhance LLM’s SQL bug-fixing abilities.

arxiv-2506-20560.creator: Shayeef Murshid, Tathagata Gupta, Vincent Russo, and
arxiv-2506-20560.description: Abstract An ensemble of product states is said to exhibit “quantum nonlocality without entanglement” if the states cannot be optimally discriminated by local operations and classical communication (LOCC). We show that this property can depend on the measure of state discrimination.

arxiv-2509-01621.title: Effects of Distributional Biases on Gradient-Based Causal Discovery in the Bivariate Categorical Case
arxiv-2509-01621.creator: Tim Schwabe tim.schwabe@tum.de, Moritz Lange moritz.lange@rub.de, Laurenz Wiskott laurenz.wiskott@rub.de, Maribel Acosta maribel.acosta@tum.de
arxiv-2509-01621.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tim Schwabe tim.schwabe@tum.de, Moritz Lange moritz.lange@rub.de, Laurenz Wiskott laurenz.wiskott@rub.de, Maribel Acosta maribel.acosta@tum.de. Gradient-based causal discovery shows great potential for deducing causal structure from data in an efficient and scalable way. Those approaches however can be susceptible to distributional biases in the data they are trained on. We identify two such biases: Marginal Distribution Asymmetry , where differences in entropy skew causal learning toward certain factorizations, and Marginal Distribution Shift Asymmetry , where repeated interventions cause faster shifts in some variables than in others.

arxiv-2511-05451.title: Sign games on graphs
arxiv-2511-05451.creator: Liz Blum, Ranjan Rohatgi
arxiv-2511-05451.description: Abstract We define the Sign Game as a two-player game played on a simple undirected mathematical graph G G . The players alternate turns, assigning vertices of G G either 1 1 or − 1 -1 , and edges take on the value of the product of their endvertices.
